regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unambiguous — until you note that PMI Composite at 55.9 is services-led (PMI Services 55.2, 84th percentile) while core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%. IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirm the investment cycle is real, but goods-economy momentum is softening at the margin. The quality question: how much of the GDP print is deflator arithmetic versus genuine output expansion in the informal economy, where two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY suggest rural demand is alive but passenger vehicle deceleration to 7.9% YoY signals urban discretionary is cooling.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 5.54% YoY is the headline — but the structure is the problem. Food inflation at 7.74% YoY has risen for two consecutive months from 3.47%, and fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY sits below the headline, which means the RBI can tell itself the underlying trend is contained — but that argument collapses the moment Brent at $110/bbl passes through to retail fuel prices. The second-order effect: WPI at this level compresses corporate margins before it shows up in CPI, and the RBI's own inflation forecast has already moved to 5.1% YoY.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence — keeps the CD ratio at 81%, the 73rd percentile historically. Services credit at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile, rising two consecutive months) and NBFC credit at 15.8% YoY (rising three consecutive months) are the accelerating engines. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held at restrictive levels, the regulator responded with risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending within two quarters. Management teams are guiding for 'granular deposit mobilisation'; CASA ratios tell a different story. Watch for a macro-prudential circular before a rate move.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, and the RBI's own GDP forecast of 6.7% YoY sits 110 basis points below the actual print — a gap that gives the committee cover to stay on hold indefinitely. The real rate, with CPI at 5.54% YoY, is effectively zero, which means monetary policy is not tight by any historical standard. For housing, an average home loan rate of 7.35% p.a. against 8% price appreciation in Bengaluru and 12% in NCR still pencils out for buyers — but the affordability index at 3.5× price-to-income is already at the 19th percentile of stress. Any further INR depreciation that forces RBI's hand would reprice mortgages before it reprices equities.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — the highest in three-plus years — make the investment cycle case straightforwardly. The inversion: capacity utilisation needs to clear 80% before private capex becomes self-sustaining without public sector anchor spending. At 77.4%, the economy is close but not there. Core sector at 4.8% YoY, slipping from 5.0%, is the early warning — cement and steel dispatch embedded in that number will tell you whether the capex signal is broadening or narrowing to a few large infrastructure projects.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month (73rd percentile) is the formalization-adjusted consumption signal — and it is stable, not accelerating. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY have decelerated for two consecutive months from 26.1%, while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY rebounded sharply. That divergence maps precisely onto the dual economy: the mass market (two-wheelers, rural) is recovering, while the urban affluent segment (passenger vehicles, e-commerce GMV at a 15th-percentile 12.4% YoY) is losing momentum. Commercial vehicle sales at 12.6% YoY, falling two consecutive months from 28.9%, suggest freight demand is softening — a leading indicator for goods-economy activity that the PMI headline does not capture.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 57th percentile. Services credit surging at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), rising 2 straight months.","implication":"The deposit-credit gap is real and structural. Banks are chasing wholesale funding and corporate deposits to fund 19%+ credit growth. Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and strong deposit franchises (HDFC Bank, Kotak). Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities — they face margin compression and refinancing risk if RBI tightens liquidity. Watch for RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level; historically, ratios >85% preceded NBFC stress (2018-19). Current divergence mirrors 2021-22 capex cycle when credit outpaced deposits by 200+ bps.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surge Signals GCC Consolidation","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, 7th percentile but up from 11.6 mn sq ft / quarter, rising 3 of last 5 quarters from 2.6→19.5 mn sq ft / quarter). Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (41st percentile, down from 14.74% vacant, falling 2 in a row). Nifty IT index flat (no directional signal). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6 / sqft / month (59th percentile, up from ₹95.9 / sqft / month). Rent in Mumbai at ₹156 / sqft / month (59th percentile, up from ₹144 / sqft / month). Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (7th percentile, strong-positive signal at 86th percentile score). Airline passengers at 86.4 mn / month (35th percentile, mild-negative signal at -30 score).","implication":"Office absorption is surging (14.1 mn sq ft / quarter) while Nifty IT is flat — this decoupling signals that Global Capability Centers (GCCs) and non-IT corporates are the real office buyers, not traditional IT services. IT services are consolidating headcount (hence flat stock), but GCCs are expanding footprint. This is a structural shift: India is becoming a hub for multinational R&D and back-office, not just outsourcing. Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% (7th percentile, 86th percentile score) is a second signal: consumption is shifting online (e-commerce GMV at 12.4% YoY, 15th percentile) but physical retail is tightening supply. Implication: (1) Overweight commercial real estate (office) plays like Embassy REIT, Mindspace REIT — they benefit from GCC expansion. (2) Underweight traditional IT services; overweight IT consulting and GCC-adjacent services (Accenture, Cognizant). (3) Retail consolidation is bullish for mall REITs — fewer, larger malls will command premium rents.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 7th percentile is historically low, but the recent surge (2.6→19.5 mn sq ft / quarter) and rising rents (Bengaluru +8%, Mumbai +8%) suggest a structural reallocation from IT to GCC/corporate. Retail vacancy at 7th percentile (4.8%) is near all-time lows — last time retail was this tight (2019), rents rose 15-20% YoY over 18 months.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But the Goods Economy Is Quietly Downshifting

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile), with PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) — both signal expansion, but services (PMI Services 55.2) is carrying the load while manufacturing (PMI Manufacturing 55.1) lags.
  • IIP Capital Goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, highest in 3+ years) confirm the investment cycle is real.
  • But core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and commercial vehicle sales fell to 12.6% YoY for the second consecutive month — freight demand is the goods economy's honest signal.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY vs passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY (falling two months) — rural mass market recovering while urban discretionary cools.

The tension: The GDP headline and the PMI agree on direction; the goods-economy proxies — core sector, CV sales, e-commerce GMV at a 15th-percentile 12.4% YoY — disagree on breadth. Services-led growth at 7.8% is real but narrower than the number implies.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a third consecutive month below 5.0% YoY would signal that the capex cycle is concentrated in public infrastructure, not broadening into private manufacturing.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Synchronised Tightening — Every Central Bank Moving, No Pivot in Sight

The facts:

  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising three consecutive months from 0.75%) — the most aggressive tightening cycle in Japan in three decades, unwinding the global carry trade's anchor.
  • Fed Funds at 3.75% p.a. and US 10Y Treasury at 5.0% yield (90th percentile) — the bond market is doing the Fed's work; real economy stress is already embedded.
  • ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (63rd percentile, rising two consecutive months), Eurozone CPI at 3.8% YoY (rising two months) — Europe has not yet broken inflation.
  • But US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile) and Global PMI Composite at 54.3 (84th percentile) signal DM growth re-acceleration — a paradox when US GDP SAAR is only 2.2%.

The tension: Survey data (PMIs at multi-year highs) and hard data (US GDP SAAR at 2.2%, decelerating) are telling opposite stories. Three central banks tightening simultaneously while surveys signal expansion is the setup for a sharp growth disappointment, not a soft landing.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underappreciated tail risk: each 25 bps move forces yen carry unwind, pressures EM FX, and tightens India's external funding conditions within 60–90 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds, But Institutional Conviction Has Repriced

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising three consecutive months — retail domestic liquidity is structurally anchored.
  • DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr net / month (95th percentile) absorbing FII equity outflows of ₹49,935 cr net / month (17th percentile) — the domestic bid is holding the market, not conviction.
  • But NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) from ₹3,051 cr / month — fund houses cannot raise fresh institutional mandates at current valuations.
  • MF average AUM at ₹87.09 lakh cr (86th percentile) but declining from ₹88.31 lakh cr — mark-to-market erosion is beginning to show in the AUM base.

The tension: SIP inflows at record levels and NFO collections at a decade low are not contradictory — they describe the same market: retail investors on autopilot, institutional allocators unwilling to commit fresh capital at these prices.

Bottom line: If FII outflows persist above ₹40,000 cr / month for a third consecutive month, DII absorption capacity will be tested — watch whether equity MF net inflows hold above ₹30,000 cr / month.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty Pricing Strength the Deposit Base Cannot Deliver

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (up 8 percentage points vs prior period), with 25% share within premium/luxury; Bengaluru, Mumbai, and NCR are the primary destinations, supported by remittances at $144.8 bn (16.2% YoY).
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum: residential sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, only 28 months unsold inventory — but the launch surge risks supply overhang within two quarters.
  • Bank Nifty at 53,975 (88th percentile) while services credit grows at 24.3% YoY — the market is pricing credit cycle strength, not the funding constraint that a CD ratio at 81% implies.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior levels — office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter has not translated into REIT price recovery.

The tension: Bank Nifty at an 88th-percentile level prices a credit upcycle; the deposit-credit divergence and REIT underperformance price a funding squeeze. One of these is wrong — and the CD ratio at 81% has historically resolved in favour of the funding constraint.

Bottom line: Avoid Bank Nifty at current levels; the risk-reward only improves if deposit growth accelerates above 19% YoY or the RBI signals macro-prudential relief on risk weights.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Fuses, One Detonator — BOJ Is Lighting the Match

The facts:

  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising three consecutive months) — yen carry unwind is the systemic risk; each 25 bps move pressures EM FX and forces FII reallocation away from India within 60–90 days.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, up from 20.05%) with Brent at $110/bbl — every $10/bbl adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill, widening CAD by ~40 bps and feeding back into CPI with a two-quarter lag.
  • India VIX at 16.403 (rising five consecutive months from 14.03) — the market's own anxiety gauge is trending, not spiking; a sustained move above 18 historically precedes institutional de-risking.
  • CD ratio at 81% (73rd percentile) with credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — if the divergence widens further, a macro-prudential circular on risk weights is the regulator's most likely response, not a rate cut.

The tension: The four risks are not independent: BOJ tightening → INR depreciation → imported fuel inflation → RBI forced to hold or hike → credit costs rise → CD ratio stress amplifies. The chain has a single trigger and four consequences.

Bottom line: Watch the BOJ's next policy meeting: a fourth consecutive hike to 1.5% p.a. would be the week's most important data point for India's FX, flows, and rate trajectory.

"}
